source: Macro Indicators Dashboard + Aug 26 Power Stack sweep
methodology: Official macro data remains the anchor, but the Aug 26 sweep adds verified developing-story overlays as directional risk lenses: AI financing quality versus physical power scarcity, refined-product versus crude tightness, El Nino second-order supply-chain risk, and selective rather than bazooka China stimulus. Secondary research is hypothesis-generating only and does not override primary data.

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.interpretation: July ISM still shows manufacturing and services expansion, but softer consumer and labour signals prevent a broad risk-on demand reading.

evidence.note: Latest official month remains July; August due Sep 1.
Latest official month remains July; August due Sep 3.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.regime: some rate relief, inflation still mixed
channels.directionMeaning: Higher = more disinflation / more room for central-bank easing
channels.interpretation: Lower bond yields and softer upstream inflation help duration, but elevated ISM price indices mean the easing case is not clean.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.regime: easing from extremes, still restrictive for long-duration capex
channels.directionMeaning: Higher = easier actual financial conditions / lower long-end yields
channels.interpretation: Bond yields have eased, but long-duration financing remains expensive. AI buildout increasingly relies on leases, SPVs, private credit, debt and customer commitments, so cost-of-capital discipline matters more than headline capex.

evidence.note: Treat off-balance-sheet commitment estimates as a stress lens, not as a substitute for company filings.
Improved from recent peaks but remains restrictive versus the prior easy-money cycle.

channels.label: Broad Credit Availability
channels.regime: available for quality borrowers; funding structure risk rising
channels.directionMeaning: Higher = tighter broad spreads / easier credit availability
channels.interpretation: Credit is still available to strong issuers, but the source and cost of financing for the next AI infrastructure leg are becoming a first-order investment variable.

evidence.note: Leases, debt, reduced buybacks, equity and third-party financing are becoming more important.

channels.label: Weak-End / Structured Credit Stress
channels.directionMeaning: Higher = MORE stress among weakest or most financing-dependent borrowers
channels.interpretation: The risk is concentrated in weak cash-flow, heavily financed or long-duration projects rather than across all investment-grade balance sheets. Penalise speculative developers and funding-dependent stories more than cash-rich incumbents.

evidence.note: Raises counterparty, refinancing and future depreciation/dilution sensitivity.

channels.label: Consumer Strength
channels.interpretation: Consumer demand remains the softer part of the macro mix, keeping discretionary and housing-sensitive exposures below industrial infrastructure on the current hierarchy.

evidence.note: Still a counterweight to strong industrial survey data.

channels.label: Housing Strength
channels.interpretation: High borrowing costs keep leveraged property and residential-cycle exposures sensitive to financing even as selected infrastructure construction remains strong.

evidence.note: Funding cost remains the main constraint.

channels.label: Industrial / Power Capex
channels.interpretation: The physical AI buildout remains strong, but the bottleneck is moving toward generation, transformers, switchgear, substations, cables, backup power and networking. Prefer contracted backlog and time-to-power beneficiaries over concept exposure.

evidence.note: Supports backup-power reliability as a real bottleneck.

channels.label: Input / Supply-Chain Pressure
channels.regime: elevated with electrical scarcity; climate tail risk rising
channels.interpretation: Copper, electrical/electronic components and other physical inputs remain constrained. A very strong El Nino raises second-order risks through export restrictions, fertilizer, hydro-to-thermal switching and freight rerouting rather than creating a simple grain trade.

evidence.note: Use as a forward supply-chain stress scenario; do not treat weather alone as the trade.

channels.label: Labour Strength
channels.directionMeaning: Higher = stronger employment and wage-income backdrop
channels.interpretation: Services employment remains weak while manufacturing employment is firmer. Labour-heavy contractors still face a less attractive margin setup than equipment suppliers with pricing power.

channels.label: Risk Appetite / Crowding
channels.interpretation: AI spending, private credit, government debt, rates and valuation are being questioned more aggressively. This is a valuation and position-sizing constraint, not evidence that physical infrastructure demand has disappeared.

evidence.note: Raise evidence threshold for high-duration and pre-commercial names.

channels.label: Crude Tightness
channels.regime: war premium fading; no broad crude shortage signal
channels.directionMeaning: Higher = tighter/higher crude balance and prices
channels.interpretation: Crude has weakened despite Iran/Hormuz headlines, so do not upgrade generic upstream beta simply because geopolitical risk remains elevated.

channels.label: Refined-Product Tightness
channels.directionMeaning: Higher = tighter product balance / wider crack spreads
channels.interpretation: The physical shortage remains more convincing in diesel, jet and gasoline than in crude. This favours refiners and product logistics tactically over indiscriminate upstream exposure.

evidence.note: Use directionally; crisis-driven margins are not permanent.

channels.label: US Gas Tightness / Thermal Switch
channels.regime: spot gas loose; forward power-demand skew improving
channels.directionMeaning: Higher = tighter/higher US natural-gas balance and prices
channels.interpretation: Current US gas is not tight enough to justify a commodity upgrade, but AI power demand and a potential El Nino hydro-to-thermal switch improve the medium-term demand skew for gas infrastructure and LNG.

evidence.note: Potential El Nino transmission channel, not yet a realised spot-gas shortage.

themes.regime: physical demand strong; financing quality and ROI now first-order

watch.title: Physical backlog versus funding quality
watch.detail: Separate real orders, customer prepayments and installed capacity from SPV/lease/private-credit financed announcements.
watch.nextTest: Hyperscaler cash flow, debt/lease disclosures, data-centre cancellations and supplier backlog conversion.

watch.title: Time to power
watch.detail: Generation, switchgear, transformers, cable, backup power and networking can outperform chip-linked beta if grid connection becomes the binding constraint.
watch.nextTest: Lead times, backlog, customer funding and grid interconnection commentary.

themes.regime: strongest structural category; scarcity and pricing power outweigh macro noise

watch.title: Scarcity versus valuation
watch.detail: The fundamental setup is strongest where backlog is contracted and equipment is difficult to substitute; entry price still matters.
watch.nextTest: GEV/PWR/ETN/TNB-style backlog, margins, lead times and cash conversion.

themes.regime: existing generation/components upgraded relative to pre-commercial developers

watch.title: Cash earnings beat optionality
watch.detail: Power scarcity strengthens nuclear, but financing risk penalises unbuilt reactors more than operating fleets, fuel and components.
watch.nextTest: Binding contracts, financing, construction milestones and operating cash flow.

themes.regime: structural scarcity intact; prefer operating/fuel-cycle quality

watch.title: Fuel-cycle economics
watch.detail: Contracting, enrichment scarcity and utility inventories remain more important than broad China stimulus or daily AI sentiment.
watch.nextTest: Long-term contracts, enrichment awards and inventory signals.

themes.regime: refined products tighter than crude; gas infrastructure gains medium-term power optionality

watch.title: Products, not just crude
watch.detail: Keep refiners/product tankers tactical while integrated majors and gas infrastructure remain the higher-quality expressions.
watch.nextTest: Crack spreads, refinery utilisation, product flows, Hormuz routing and gas-to-power demand.

watch.title: El Nino thermal switch
watch.detail: Hydro weakness can raise LNG, gas, coal and tanker tonne-miles, but only if rainfall and grid substitution evidence confirms it.
watch.nextTest: Hydro reservoir data, LNG demand, canal restrictions and freight rates.

themes.regime: copper structurally supported; China demand prevents indiscriminate cyclical upgrades

watch.title: Copper remains the cleanest metal
watch.detail: Grid and electrical scarcity support copper, while China's just-enough policy stance argues against treating all industrial metals as a stimulus trade.
watch.nextTest: Inventories, treatment charges, Chinese demand and grid capex.

themes.regime: commercial ROI favoured over humanoid duration

watch.title: Deployment evidence first
watch.detail: Warehouse automation and machine vision rank above pre-scale humanoids because customer ROI and cash economics are observable now.
watch.nextTest: Orders, deployments, customer concentration and positive cash conversion.
